title: The Part of a Resident Funds Transfer That Reached an Ancillary Charge
content:
A payer-covered return to a Resident Trust Fund Accounts account never exceeds the transfer's paid part: the part of the transfer that actually paid the ancillary charge it named. For a transfer not already returned for lacking authorization or as a duplicate, the paid part follows how the transfer reached the charge, as the ledger of the resident's Ancillary and Optional Services Billing account and the account's signed requests show.

## The rule

| What the records show | Transfer's paid part |
|---|---|
| the ancillary ledger carries a payment by trust transfer naming the charge on the transfer's date | that payment, never more than the transfer less the wrong-amount returns already made from it, because the ancillary account applies a payment only up to the charge's open balance |
| it carries none, and a per-bill authorization names the charge | the amount the most recent such authorization states, because a transfer pays no more than its authorization and any excess is returned as a wrong amount |
| otherwise | the whole transfer |

## Hypothetical illustration

A transfer of $75.00 named an ancillary charge.

| Records | Paid part |
|---|---|
| ancillary ledger: trust-transfer payment of $61.20 on the transfer's date; no wrong-amount return | $61.20 |
| same payment; a wrong-amount return of $14.60 already made from the transfer | $60.40 (the transfer less the return is lower than the payment) |
| no such payment; the most recent per-bill authorization naming the charge states $68.00 | $68.00 |
| no such payment and no authorization naming the charge | $75.00 |
